correctness.rationale: The Petersen adjacency satisfies \(A^2=2I-A+J\). The continuous-time heat semigroup therefore has nonconstant eigenrates 2 and 5 and an exact pair-difference formula. Real-signal layer-cake reduces its quotient norm to binary cuts. All 1022 nontrivial cuts, independently partitioned into 32 symmetry orbits, are exhaustively evaluated using integer arithmetic: \(G((A+2I)\mathbf1_S)\le(11/3)|S|(10-|S|)\), strict except singleton/complement. Convexity in \(r=e^{-3t}\) and \((A+2I)+(I-A)=3I\) yield an inequality for every real \(t\ge0\), with singleton equality. The three orbit values of the heat kernel give the exact Dobrushin coefficient and strict gap. This is a complete finite lemma plus analytical continuum proof, not extrapolation from sampled times.

originality.rationale: The 2013 Gaubert–Qu source gives the Doeblin–Dobrushin coefficient for oscillation and dual total variation. For the Petersen semigroup, that coefficient is \(\delta(t)=(4e^{-2t}-e^{-5t})/3\), whereas the proved complete-pair Gini coefficient is \(\gamma(t)=(11e^{-2t}-2e^{-5t})/9\). Their gap is strictly positive for every positive time; hence the general theorem is not covering this exact norm. published-finding corpus, accessible historical claims, and public literature searches under Petersen/heat/pairwise-variation aliases returned no stated equivalent exact coefficient. The nearest records concern different operators, norms or numerical discretizations. This is best-knowledge originality, not certified priority.

value.rationale: For the canonical ten-state cubic strongly regular Petersen diffusion, this is the full exact continuous-time Gini contraction curve with singleton cut rigidity and a proved strict quantitative separation from the classic Dobrushin oscillation coefficient. Such an all-time stability benchmark, identifying exact initial decay and asymptotic spectral prefactor, has a natural role in assessing graph consensus/smoothing beyond generic spectral or oscillation bounds. It is more informative than a one-off table coefficient or a routine normalization calculation. The finite graph scope is acknowledged, and no broader graph-family theorem is claimed.
